newsitem.title: PERU: Peru captures key Shining Path leaders - sources.
newsitem.headline: Peru captures key Shining Path leaders - sources.

text.p: Peruvian security forces have captured the military leaders of two key Maoist Shining Path units during a massive operation in the guerrillas' jungle heartland, anti-terrorist police sources said on Thursday.
The sweep, which has been going on for a week, also brought the biggest guerrilla arms haul in Peru since the start of Shining Path's uprising in 1980, the sources added.

The army caught the leaders of two 200-strong armed units responsible for controlling the dense jungle around Mohena and Pucayacu, 200 miles (320 km) northeast of Lima, where Shining Path's highest decision-making body operates, the sources said.
"Here it is not soldiers that have been caught, it is generals," one police source said.
The army also located several large arms caches, capturing more than 30 anti-tank rockets, a few anti-aircraft rockets, one mortar, more than 30 rifles, 300 grenades and 9,000 bullets.
"We have taken the largest amount of arms and ammunition in the whole anti-terrorist fight," one source said. "Their armed power has suffered a tremendous blow."
